mock_data.title: Climate Strikes Grow Up
mock_data.passage:
A New Scientist comment article by Alice Bell about the climate strike movement expanding from youth to adults.

It is just over a year since Swedish teenager Greta Thunberg, frustrated by political inaction on climate change and following Sweden's hottest summer in more than 250 years, skipped school and sat in front of the Swedish parliament with a handwritten "Skolstrejk för klimatet" (School strike for the climate) sign.

Before long, teenagers in other countries were following her lead, building momentum towards the global Fridays for Future school strike movement. They have brought a new energy, bluntness and charisma to the climate debate – and shown spectacular skill at embarrassing politicians.

On 20 September, they are asking adults all over the world to join them in showing up on the streets. Whether you are an employee, employer or neither, it's worth asking what you can do to answer that call.

If nothing else, this is a chance to show a positive spirit of intergenerational cooperation on an issue that could be very generationally divisive – and in a world increasingly scarred by such conflict. Climate change is an issue for us all. We should send a clear signal that we know delegating it to the young to sort out will leave it too late.

Australia shows how support can be mobilised. It was one of the first places outside Sweden to spark a youth strike. By dint of their nation's location on the globe, Australians will be some of the first to strike. There, the Not Business As Usual coalition of employers has pledged to support the strike, whether by closing company doors, having a meeting-free day, allowing a longer lunch break to attend protests or just making it clear that teams won't be penalised for taking a few hours off.

In the UK, the Trades Union Congress has voted to support 30 minutes of solidarity action on the day. As the strike begins across the Atlantic, more than 1000 employees at Amazon will also walk out, part of the long-standing Amazon Employees for Climate Justice campaign.

If you can't leave work, there are still plenty of ways to aid the strikers. You could donate some of your wages to a climate campaign or write to schools, local papers and political representatives in support of the protests.

Above all, the young strikers want to see more people taking increasingly ambitious climate action. The most helpful thing any of us can do is look around, decide what needs to change and resolve to make that change happen.

That can't end with a 30-minute microstrike on 20 September. Climate change isn't something we simply win or lose, then the game ends. As climate scientist Kate Marvel puts it, it's more of a slope we slide down.

The sort of climate nihilism that the novelist Jonathan Franzen was pilloried for after his article in The New Yorker last week – that we're doomed, so there's no point doing anything – is the last thing we need right now. As we cross the threshold of 1°C of global warming, it's still not too late. Concerted, sustained action on behalf of all those who care about the future of the planet is what is needed. 20 September is the perfect time to show that's where you stand, too.
mock_data.passageB1:
More than a year ago, a Swedish teenager called Greta Thunberg was upset because politicians were not doing enough about climate change. Sweden had just had its hottest summer in over 250 years. So, Greta decided to take action. She stopped going to school and sat in front of the Swedish parliament with a sign that said "School strike for the climate".

Soon, other teenagers in different countries started doing the same thing. This grew into a big movement called Fridays for Future. These young people have brought new energy and a direct way of speaking to the climate discussion. They have also been very good at making politicians feel embarrassed.

On September 20th, they are asking adults all over the world to join them in protesting in the streets. If you work, own a business, or don't work, it's a good idea to think about what you can do to help.

This is a chance to show that different generations can work together on a problem that could cause conflict between them. Climate change affects everyone. We need to show that we know it will be too late if we only let young people deal with it.

Australia shows how people can be motivated to help. It was one of the first countries outside Sweden where young people started striking. Because of where Australia is on the Earth, Australians will be among the first to strike. There, a group of employers called Not Business As Usual has promised to support the strike. They will do this by closing their businesses, having days without meetings, allowing longer lunch breaks for people to go to protests, or simply making it clear that workers will not be punished for taking a few hours off.

In the UK, the Trades Union Congress has voted to support 30 minutes of action on that day. When the strike starts in America, more than 1000 workers at Amazon will also protest, as part of the Amazon Employees for Climate Justice campaign.

If you can't leave work, there are still many ways to help the strikers. You could give some of your money to a climate campaign, or write to schools, local newspapers, and politicians to support the protests.

Most of all, the young strikers want to see more people taking stronger climate action. The most helpful thing anyone can do is to look around, decide what needs to change, and promise to make that change happen.

This can't just be a 30-minute protest on September 20th. Climate change is not something we can simply win or lose. A climate scientist named Kate Marvel says it's like a slope we are sliding down.

The idea that we are doomed and there's no point in doing anything, is the last thing we need right now. We have already reached 1°C of global warming, but it's still not too late. We need everyone who cares about the future of the planet to take strong, consistent action. September 20th is the perfect time to show that you are one of those people. It’s time to take a stand.
mock_data.passageB2:
Just over a year ago, Greta Thunberg, a Swedish teenager, took a stand against the lack of action on climate change. After Sweden experienced its hottest summer in over 250 years, she decided to skip school and protest outside the Swedish parliament with a sign that read "School strike for the climate."

Soon, young people in other countries followed her example, creating the global Fridays for Future school strike movement. They have brought a fresh, direct, and compelling voice to the climate debate. They have also been remarkably successful at highlighting the failures of politicians.

On September 20th, they are asking adults worldwide to join them in protesting. Whether you are employed, an employer, or neither, it's important to consider how you can respond to their call. This is a chance to demonstrate solidarity and cooperation between generations on an issue that could easily divide them. Climate change affects everyone, and we need to show that leaving it to young people alone will mean action comes too late.

Australia provides an example of how support can be mobilized. It was one of the first countries outside Sweden where youth strikes began. Because of its geographical location, Australia will be among the first to strike. There, the Not Business As Usual coalition, made up of employers, has promised to support the strike. This support includes closing company offices, holding meeting-free days, allowing longer lunch breaks for protest attendance, or simply making it clear that employees won't be penalized for taking a few hours off.

In the UK, the Trades Union Congress has voted to support 30 minutes of collective action on the day. As the strike begins across the Atlantic, over 1000 Amazon employees will also strike, as part of the Amazon Employees for Climate Justice campaign, which has been going on for some time.

If you can't leave work, you can still support the strikers in other ways. You could donate part of your salary to a climate change campaign or write to schools, local newspapers, and politicians to support the protests. You can also raise awareness by sharing information on social media.

Above all, the young strikers want to see more people taking decisive climate action. The most helpful thing we can all do is assess the situation, identify what needs to change, and commit to making that change happen. This can involve adopting sustainable practices in your everyday life or lobbying for policy changes.

This effort cannot end with a 30-minute strike on September 20th. Climate change is not a problem we simply solve and then move on. As climate scientist Kate Marvel says, it's more like a slippery slope. We need continuous effort.

The kind of climate pessimism expressed by novelist Jonathan Franzen, suggesting that we are doomed so action is pointless, is the last thing we need right now. Even as we pass the 1°C global warming threshold, it is still not too late. Coordinated, sustained action from everyone who cares about the planet's future is essential. September 20th is the ideal opportunity to show where you stand and demonstrate your commitment to this cause. Don't miss the chance to make a difference!
mock_data.passageC1:
Barely a year has elapsed since Greta Thunberg, then a Swedish teenager driven by her frustration with political inertia regarding climate change, and catalyzed by Sweden's unprecedentedly hot summer, initiated her solitary protest. By absenting herself from school and staging a sit-in before the Swedish parliament, brandishing a handwritten sign declaring "Skolstrejk för klimatet" (School strike for the climate), Thunberg unwittingly set in motion a global phenomenon.

Before long, her actions resonated with adolescents internationally, galvanizing a worldwide Fridays for Future school strike movement. These young activists have infused the climate discourse with a fresh dynamism, a refreshing candor, and a captivating charisma, while simultaneously demonstrating a remarkable aptitude for putting politicians on the spot. Their influence has been undeniable, forcing a re-evaluation of climate action strategies globally.

On September 20th, these very students are extending an invitation to adults worldwide to lend their support by joining them in a collective demonstration. Whether one is an employee, an employer, or neither, it behooves each individual to consider how they might heed this call and contribute to the cause. This is not merely a symbolic gesture, but a tangible opportunity to foster a spirit of intergenerational cooperation on a matter that, if mishandled, risks engendering profound generational discord. Climate change, after all, is a universal concern. We must collectively signal that entrusting its resolution solely to the younger generation would, in all likelihood, prove a fatal miscalculation.

Australia offers a compelling illustration of how such support can be effectively mobilized. As one of the first nations outside Sweden to witness the emergence of youth-led strikes, Australia, by virtue of its geographical location, will be among the first to participate in this global action. There, the Not Business As Usual coalition, comprising a diverse array of employers, has pledged its allegiance to the strike. Their commitment manifests in various forms, ranging from temporarily suspending business operations to designating meeting-free days, granting extended lunch breaks for protest participation, or simply assuring employees that their involvement in the strike will not incur penalties. This proactive stance exemplifies a willingness to disrupt the status quo for the sake of a greater environmental good.

In the UK, the Trades Union Congress has formally endorsed a 30-minute act of solidarity on the designated day. Concurrently, as the strike gains traction across the Atlantic, over 1000 Amazon employees are poised to stage a walkout, representing an escalation of the longstanding Amazon Employees for Climate Justice campaign. This collective action underscores the growing recognition within the corporate sector of the imperative to address climate change.

Even for those whose professional obligations preclude their physical presence at the strike, numerous avenues remain open to contribute to the cause. One could consider allocating a portion of their earnings to a climate-focused campaign, or alternatively, articulate their support for the protests through letters addressed to schools, local media outlets, and elected officials. Such actions, while seemingly modest, can collectively amplify the message and exert pressure on decision-makers.

Ultimately, the overarching aspiration of the young strikers is to witness a broader segment of the population embracing increasingly ambitious climate action. The most impactful contribution any individual can make lies in critically evaluating their surroundings, identifying areas ripe for change, and resolutely committing to catalyzing that transformation. This cannot be a fleeting gesture confined to a 30-minute “microstrike” on September 20th. Climate change is not a discrete challenge with a definitive resolution; rather, as climate scientist Kate Marvel aptly observes, it resembles a slope down which we are inexorably sliding.

The brand of climate nihilism espoused by novelist Jonathan Franzen in his recent New Yorker article – the defeatist notion that our fate is sealed, rendering all efforts futile – is precisely the mindset we must actively resist. Even as we breach the threshold of 1°C of global warming, it is still not too late to avert the most catastrophic consequences. Concerted, sustained action, undertaken on behalf of all who hold the planet's future dear, is the sine qua non. September 20th presents an unparalleled opportunity to unequivocally declare one's commitment to this vital cause.

mock_data.translation:
Iqlim ish tashlash harakati yoshlardan kattalarga kengayishi haqida Alice Bell tomonidan yozilgan New Scientist sharh maqolasi.

Shvediyalik o'smir Greta Tunberg iqlim o'zgarishi bo'yicha siyosiy harakatsizlikdan norozilanib va Shvediyaning 250 yildan ortiq vaqt ichidagi eng issiq yozidan so'ng, maktabni tashlab, shved parlamenti oldida "Skolstrejk för klimatet" (Iqlim uchun maktab ish tashlashi) degan qo'lda yozilgan plakat bilan o'tirganiga bir yildan sal ko'proq bo'ldi.

Ko'p o'tmay, boshqa mamlakatlardagi o'smirlar uning yo'lidan borib, global Fridays for Future maktab ish tashlash harakatiga tomon tezlikni oshirdilar. Ular iqlim munozarasiga yangi energiya, ochiqlik va jozibadorlik olib keldilar – va siyosatchilrani uyaltirish bo'yicha ajoyib mahorat ko'rsatdilar.

20 sentabrda ular butun dunyo bo'ylab kattalarni ko'chalarga chiqishga qo'shilishlarini so'rashmoqda. Siz xodim, ish beruvchi yoki hech biri bo'lmasangiz ham, bu chaqiruvga javob berish uchun nima qila olishingizni so'rash arziydi.

Boshqa hech narsa bo'lmasa-da, bu avlodlararo hamkorlikning ijobiy ruhini ko'rsatish imkoniyatidir – bu avlodlar o'rtasida juda bo'linuvchan bo'lishi mumkin bo'lgan masalada – va bunday mojarolar tufayli tobora ko'proq jarohatlanayotgan dunyoda. Iqlim o'zgarishi barchamiz uchun muammo. Biz buni yoshlarga topshirib, hal qilishga qo'yish juda kech bo'lishini bilamiz degan aniq signal yuborishimiz kerak.

Avstraliya qo'llab-quvvatlashni qanday safarbar qilish mumkinligini ko'rsatadi. U Shvediyadan tashqarida yoshlar ish tashlashini boshlagan birinchi joylardan biri edi. O'z mamlakatining globusdagi joylashuvi tufayli avstraliyaliklar birinchi bo'lib ish tashlashga chiqqanlardan bo'ladi. U yerda Not Business As Usual ish beruvchilar koalitsiyasi ish tashlashni qo'llab-quvvatlashga va'da berdi – kompaniya eshiklarini yopish, uchrashusiz kun o'tkazish, noroziliklarda qatnashish uchun uzoqroq tushlik tanaffusiga ruxsat berish yoki jamoalar bir necha soat dam olganlik uchun jazolanmasligini aniq qilish orqali.

Buyuk Britaniyada Kasaba uyushmalari Kongressi shu kuni 30 daqiqalik birdamlik aksiyasini qo'llab-quvvatlashga ovoz berdi. Ish tashlash Atlantika bo'ylab boshlanayotganda, Amazondagi 1000 dan ortiq xodim ham chiqib ketadi – bu Amazon Xodimlari Iqlim Adolati kampaniyasining bir qismi.

Agar siz ishdan chiqib keta olmasangiz, ish tashlashchilarga yordam berishning ko'plab yo'llari bor. Siz maoshingizning bir qismini iqlim kampaniyasiga xayriya qilishingiz yoki maktablarga, mahalliy gazetalarga va siyosiy vakillarga noroziliklarga qo'llab-quvvatlash maktubini yozishingiz mumkin.

Eng muhimi, yosh ish tashlashchilar ko'proq odamlarning tobora shuhratparastroq iqlim harakatlarini ko'rishni xohlashadi. Har birimiz qila oladigan eng foydali narsa – atrofga qarab, nimani o'zgartirish kerakligini hal qilish va bu o'zgarishni amalga oshirishga qaror qilishdir.

Bu 20 sentabrdagi 30 daqiqalik mikro ish tashlash bilan tugashi mumkin emas. Iqlim o'zgarishi biz oddiy g'olib bo'ladigan yoki yengiladigan, keyin o'yin tugaydigan narsa emas. Iqlim olimi Keyt Marvel aytganidek, bu ko'proq biz pastga sirpanib tushadigan nishabga o'xshaydi.

Romanchi Jonatan Franzen o'tgan hafta The New Yorker jurnalida maqolasidan keyin koyilgan iqlim nigilizmi – biz halok bo'lamiz, shuning uchun biror narsa qilishning ma'nosi yo'q – hozir bizga kerak bo'lgan eng oxirgi narsa. Global isish 1°C chegarasini kesib o'tayotganimizda, hali juda kech emas. Sayyoramiz kelajagiga g'amxo'rlik qiladigan barcha nomidan kelishilgan, tinimsiz harakat kerak. 20 sentabr – siz ham qayerda turganingizni ko'rsatish uchun eng yaxshi vaqt.

mock_data.translationB1:
Bir yildan ko'proq vaqt oldin, Greta Tunberg ismli shvetsiyalik o'smir siyosatchilar iqlim o'zgarishi bo'yicha yetarli ish qilmayotganidan xafa edi. Shvetsiyada so'nggi 250 yildan ortiq vaqtdagi eng issiq yoz bo'lgandi. Shunday qilib, Greta chora ko'rishga qaror qildi. U maktabga borishni to'xtatdi va Shvetsiya parlamenti oldida "Iqlim uchun maktab tashlashi" degan yozuvli plakat bilan o'tirdi.

Tez orada boshqa mamlakatlardagi o'smirlar ham xuddi shunday ish qilishni boshladilar. Bu "Kelajak uchun juma kunlari" deb nomlangan katta harakatga aylandi. Bu yoshlar iqlim muhokamasiga yangi energiya va to'g'ridan-to'g'ri so'zlash uslubini olib kelishdi. Ular, shuningdek, siyosatchilarni uyaltirishda juda yaxshi bo'lishdi.

20-sentabr kuni ular butun dunyo bo'ylab kattalardan ko'chalarda namoyish o'tkazishda ularga qo'shilishni so'rashmoqda. Agar siz ishlasangiz, biznesingiz bo'lsa yoki ishlamasangiz, yordam berish uchun nima qilishingiz mumkinligi haqida o'ylab ko'rish yaxshi fikr.

Bu turli avlodlar ular o'rtasida nizoga sabab bo'lishi mumkin bo'lgan muammo ustida birgalikda ishlashi mumkinligini ko'rsatish uchun imkoniyat. Iqlim o'zgarishi hammaga ta'sir qiladi. Faqat yoshlarga hal qilishga qo'yib bersak, juda kech bo'lishini bilishimizni ko'rsatishimiz kerak.

Avstraliya odamlarning yordam berishga qanday rag'batlantirilishi mumkinligini ko'rsatadi. Bu Shvetsiyadan tashqaridagi yoshlar ish tashlashni boshlagan birinchi davlatlardan biri edi. Avstraliyaning Yer yuzida joylashgan o'rniga ko'ra, avstraliyaliklar birinchilardan bo'lib ish tashlashadi. U yerda "Odatdagidek biznes emas" deb nomlangan ish beruvchilar guruhi ish tashlashni qo'llab-quvvatlashga va'da berdi. Ular buni o'z bizneslarini yopish, uchrashuvlarsiz kunlar o'tkazish, odamlarga namoyishlarga borish uchun uzoqroq tushlik tanaffuslari berish yoki shunchaki ishchilarning bir necha soat dam olishi uchun jazolanmasligini aniq ko'rsatish orqali amalga oshiradilar.

Buyuk Britaniyada Kasaba uyushmalari kongressi o'sha kuni 30 daqiqalik harakatni qo'llab-quvvatlash uchun ovoz berdi. Amerikada ish tashlash boshlanganda, Amazonning 1000 dan ortiq ishchilari ham "Iqlim adolati uchun Amazon xodimlari" kampaniyasining bir qismi sifatida norozilik bildirishadi.

Agar siz ishdan ketolmasangiz, ish tashlashchilarga yordam berishning ko'plab usullari mavjud. Siz iqlim kampaniyasiga pulingizning bir qismini berishingiz yoki maktablarga, mahalliy gazetalarga va siyosatchilarga namoyishlarni qo'llab-quvvatlash uchun xat yozishingiz mumkin.

Eng muhimi, yosh ish tashlashchilar ko'proq odamlarning iqlim bo'yicha kuchliroq harakat qilishini ko'rishni xohlashadi. Har kim qilishi mumkin bo'lgan eng foydali narsa - atrofga qarash, nima o'zgarishi kerakligini hal qilish va o'sha o'zgarishni amalga oshirishga va'da berishdir.

Bu shunchaki 20-sentabr kuni 30 daqiqalik namoyish bo'lishi mumkin emas. Iqlim o'zgarishi shunchaki yutish yoki yutqazish mumkin bo'lgan narsa emas. Keyt Marvel ismli iqlimshunosning aytishicha, bu biz sirpanayotgan qiyalikka o'xshaydi.

Biz halok bo'lganmiz va hech narsa qilishning ma'nosi yo'q degan fikr - hozir bizga eng kerak bo'lmagan narsa. Biz allaqachon global isishning 1°C darajasiga yetdik, lekin hali ham kech emas. Sayyoramiz kelajagiga befarq bo'lmagan har bir kishi kuchli, izchil harakat qilishi kerak. 20-sentabr - siz o'sha odamlardan biri ekanligingizni ko'rsatish uchun ajoyib vaqt. O'z pozitsiyangizni bildirish vaqti keldi.

Xuddi bir yil oldin, shved oʻsmiri Greta Tunberg iqlim oʻzgarishiga qarshi yetarli choralar koʻrilmayotganiga e’tiroz bildirdi. Shvetsiyada 250 yildan ortiq vaqt ichida eng issiq yoz kuzatilgandan soʻng, u maktabni qoldirib, Shvetsiya parlamenti oldida "Iqlim uchun maktab ish tashlashi" degan yozuvli plakat bilan norozilik bildirishga qaror qildi.

Tez orada boshqa mamlakatlardagi yoshlar ham uning namunasiga ergashib, Fridays for Future global maktab ish tashlashi harakatini yaratdilar. Ular iqlim boʻyicha bahslarga yangi, bevosita va ta’sirchan ovoz olib keldilar. Ular, shuningdek, siyosatchilarning xatolarini ta’kidlashda juda muvaffaqiyatli boʻlishdi.

20-sentabr kuni ular butun dunyo boʻylab kattalarni norozilik bildirishda ularga qoʻshilishga chaqirmoqda. Ishlasangiz ham, ish beruvchi boʻlsangiz ham, yoki hech qaysisi boʻlmasangiz ham, ularning chaqirigʻiga qanday javob berishingiz mumkinligini koʻrib chiqish muhim. Bu avlodlar oʻrtasida ularni osonlik bilan ajratib qoʻyishi mumkin boʻlgan masalada birdamlik va hamkorlikni namoyish etish imkoniyatidir. Iqlim oʻzgarishi hammaga ta’sir qiladi va biz buni faqat yoshlarga qoldirish harakatning juda kech kelishini anglatishini koʻrsatishimiz kerak.

Avstraliya yordamni qanday safarlashtirish mumkinligiga misol boʻla oladi. Bu Shvetsiyadan tashqari yoshlar ish tashlashlari boshlangan birinchi davlatlardan biri edi. Geografik joylashuvi tufayli Avstraliya birinchilardan boʻlib ish tashlaydi. U yerda ish beruvchilardan tashkil topgan Not Business As Usual koalitsiyasi ish tashlashni qoʻllab-quvvatlashga va’da berdi. Bu qoʻllab-quvvatlash kompaniya ofislarini yopishni, uchrashuvsiz kunlarni oʻtkazishni, norozilik namoyishlarida qatnashish uchun tushlik tanaffuslarini uzaytirishni yoki shunchaki xodimlarning bir necha soat dam olishlari uchun jazolanmasligini aniqlashtirishni oʻz ichiga oladi.

Buyuk Britaniyada Trades Union Congress oʻsha kuni 30 daqiqalik jamoaviy harakatni qoʻllab-quvvatlash uchun ovoz berdi. Ish tashlash Atlantika okeani boʻylab boshlanar ekan, Amazon’ning 1000 dan ortiq xodimi ham Amazon Employees for Climate Justice kampaniyasi doirasida ish tashlaydi, bu kampaniya ancha vaqtdan beri davom etmoqda.

Agar siz ishni tashlab keta olmasangiz, ish tashlashchilarni boshqa yoʻllar bilan qoʻllab-quvvatlashingiz mumkin. Siz ish haqingizning bir qismini iqlim oʻzgarishi kampaniyasiga xayriya qilishingiz yoki maktablarga, mahalliy gazetalar va siyosatchilarga norozilik namoyishlarini qoʻllab-quvvatlash uchun xat yozishingiz mumkin. Shuningdek, ijtimoiy tarmoqlarda ma’lumot almashish orqali xabardorlikni oshirishingiz mumkin.

Eng muhimi, yosh ish tashlashchilar koʻproq odamlarning qat’iy iqlimiy harakatlarni amalga oshirishini koʻrishni xohlashadi. Biz hammamiz qiladigan eng foydali narsa - vaziyatni baholash, nima oʻzgarishi kerakligini aniqlash va oʻsha oʻzgarishni amalga oshirishga sodiq qolishdir. Bu sizning kundalik hayotingizda barqaror amaliyotlarni qabul qilishni yoki siyosat oʻzgarishi uchun lobbichilik qilishni oʻz ichiga olishi mumkin.

Bu harakat 20-sentabr kuni 30 daqiqalik ish tashlash bilan tugamasligi kerak. Iqlim oʻzgarishi shunchaki yechib, keyin davom etadigan muammo emas. Iqlimshunos Keyt Marvel aytganidek, bu koʻproq sirpanchiq qiyalikga oʻxshaydi. Biz doimiy harakat qilishimiz kerak.

Yozuvchi Jonatan Frannzen tomonidan ifodalangan iqlimiy tushkunlik, ya’ni bizning qismatimiz hal boʻlgani uchun harakat qilishning ma’nosi yoʻq degan fikr, hozir bizga eng kam kerak boʻlgan narsadir. Biz 1°C global isish chegarasidan oʻtayotgan boʻlsak ham, hali kech emas. Sayyoramiz kelajagiga befarq boʻlmagan har bir kishining muvofiqlashtirilgan, doimiy harakati juda muhim. 20-sentabr sizning pozitsiyangizni koʻrsatish va bu ishga sodiqligingizni namoyish etish uchun ideal imkoniyatdir. Oʻzgartirish kiritish imkoniyatini qoʻldan boy bermang!

Greta Tunberg, o'sha paytda Shvetsiyalik o'smir, iqlim o'zgarishi bo'yicha siyosiy befarqlikdan g'azablangan va Shvetsiyaning misli ko'rilmagan issiq yozidan ta'sirlangan holda, o'zining yakka norozilik harakatini boshlaganiga bir yil ham o'tmadi. U maktabga bormay, Shvetsiya parlamentining oldida "Skolstrejk för klimatet" (Iqlim uchun maktab ish tashlashi) deb yozilgan qo'lyozma plakat bilan o'tirib, Tunberg o'zi bilmagan holda global hodisani boshlab yubordi.

Ko'p o'tmay, uning harakatlari xalqaro miqyosdagi o'smirlarning e'tiborini tortdi va butun dunyo bo'ylab Fridays for Future maktab ish tashlashi harakatini kuchaytirdi. Bu yosh faollar iqlim munozarasiga yangi dinamizm, tetiklantiruvchi samimiylik va jozibali xarizma olib kirdi, shu bilan birga siyosatchilarni noqulay vaziyatga solish qobiliyatini ham namoyish etdi. Ularning ta'siri inkor etib bo'lmaydi, bu butun dunyo bo'ylab iqlim bo'yicha harakat strategiyalarini qayta ko'rib chiqishga majbur qildi.

20-sentabr kuni aynan shu talabalar butun dunyo bo'ylab kattalarni ommaviy namoyishda ularga qo'shilish orqali qo'llab-quvvatlashga taklif qilmoqda. Xodim bo'lasizmi, ish beruvchi bo'lasizmi yoki umuman hech kim emasmi, har bir shaxs bu chaqiriqqa qanday javob berish va bu ishga qanday hissa qo'shish mumkinligi haqida o'ylab ko'rishi kerak. Bu shunchaki ramziy imo-ishora emas, balki, agar noto'g'ri hal qilinsa, avlodlar o'rtasida chuqur kelishmovchilikni keltirib chiqarish xavfi bo'lgan masalada avlodlararo hamkorlik ruhini uyg'otish uchun aniq imkoniyatdir. Axir, iqlim o'zgarishi - bu umumiy tashvish. Biz uning yechimini faqat yosh avlodga topshirish, ehtimol, halokatli xato bo'lishini hammamiz birgalikda ko'rsatishimiz kerak.

Avstraliya bunday yordamni qanday qilib samarali safarbar qilish mumkinligiga ishonchli misol bo'la oladi. Shvetsiyadan tashqari yoshlar boshchiligidagi ish tashlashlar paydo bo'lgan birinchi davlatlardan biri sifatida, Avstraliya geografik joylashuvi tufayli ushbu global aksiyada birinchi bo'lib ishtirok etadi. U erda turli xil ish beruvchilardan iborat Not Business As Usual koalitsiyasi ish tashlashga sodiqligini bildirdi. Ularning sadoqati turli shakllarda namoyon bo'ladi, jumladan biznes operatsiyalarini vaqtincha to'xtatib turishdan tortib, uchrashuvsiz kunlarni belgilash, norozilikda ishtirok etish uchun uzoqroq tushlik tanaffuslarini berish yoki shunchaki xodimlarning ish tashlashda ishtirok etishi jarimaga sabab bo'lmasligiga ishonch hosil qilish. Ushbu faol pozitsiya atrof-muhitning katta yaxshiligi uchun mavjud holatni buzishga tayyor ekanlikni ko'rsatadi.

Buyuk Britaniyada Kasaba uyushmalari kongressi belgilangan kuni 30 daqiqalik birdamlik harakatini rasman qo'llab-quvvatladi. Shu bilan birga, ish tashlash Atlantika okeani bo'ylab kuchayib borar ekan, 1000 dan ortiq Amazon xodimlari ish tashlashga tayyorlanmoqda, bu esa uzoq vaqtdan beri davom etayotgan Amazon Employees for Climate Justice kampaniyasining kuchayganini anglatadi. Ushbu jamoaviy harakat korporativ sektorda iqlim o'zgarishiga e'tibor qaratish zarurligi haqida tobora ortib borayotgan e'tirofni ta'kidlaydi.

Hatto kasbiy majburiyatlari tufayli ish tashlashda jismonan ishtirok eta olmaydiganlar uchun ham bu ishga hissa qo'shishning ko'plab imkoniyatlari mavjud. O'z daromadlarining bir qismini iqlimga yo'naltirilgan kampaniyaga ajratish yoki maktablarga, mahalliy ommaviy axborot vositalariga va saylangan rasmiylarga yo'llagan xatlar orqali noroziliklarni qo'llab-quvvatlashni ifoda etish mumkin. Bunday harakatlar, garchi unchalik katta bo'lmasa ham, birgalikda xabarni kuchaytirishi va qaror qabul qiluvchilarga bosim o'tkazishi mumkin.

Oxir oqibat, yosh ish tashlashchilarning asosiy maqsadi aholining katta qismining tobora ambitsiyali iqlim harakatini qo'llab-quvvatlashiga guvoh bo'lishdir. Har bir shaxs qo'sha oladigan eng katta hissa - bu o'z atrofini tanqidiy baholash, o'zgarishga tayyor bo'lgan sohalarni aniqlash va shu o'zgarishni boshlashga qat'iy qaror qilishdir. Bu 20-sentabr kuni 30 daqiqalik "mikro-ish tashlash" bilan cheklangan vaqtincha imo-ishora bo'lishi mumkin emas. Iqlim o'zgarishi - bu aniq yechimga ega bo'lgan alohida muammo emas; aksincha, iqlimshunos olim Keyt Marvel ta'kidlaganidek, bu biz qiyalik bo'ylab tinimsiz sirpanayotganlikka o'xshaydi.

Yozuvchi Jonatan Frantsen o'zining yaqinda New Yorker jurnalida chop etilgan maqolasida ilgari surgan iqlim nihilizm brendi - bizning taqdirimiz muhrlangan, barcha harakatlar befoyda degan mag'lubiyatparastona tushunchaga biz faol qarshilik ko'rsatishimiz kerak. Biz global isishning 1°C chegarasidan o'tsak ham, eng falokatli oqibatlarning oldini olish hali ham kech emas. Sayyoramiz kelajagini qadrlaydigan barcha odamlar nomidan qilingan birgalikdagi, uzluksiz harakat - bu zarur shartdir. 20-sentabr ushbu muhim ishga sodiqligini aniq bildirish uchun beqiyos imkoniyat taqdim etadi.
